data.name: Raghubir
data.gender_notes: Raghubir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who rules the heart, Raghu (ruler) + Bhrat (brother or protector). The name Raghubir carries the meaning “King of the Heart” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Raghubir usually hope their child will grow to embody king of the heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner king and the protector of the heart
data.etymology: Raghubir belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of the Heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raghubir total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Raghubir" holds a significant cultural importance in Hindu society as it is the name of a renowned king from the Ikshvaku dynasty, Raghu Raja, who is considered an ideal ruler and guardian. This name reflects the strong cultural value of a just and kind monarch who protects his people and governs with wisdom and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Raghubir" also holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus as it represents the divine guardian of the heart, signifying the inner ruler and protector. This name inspires one to cultivate purity in both heart and thought, reflecting the spiritual virtue of controlling the senses and nurturing the soul with devotion and selflessness. It is believed that through the chanting of this name, the Divine Protector, Raghubir, blesses His devotees with strength, courage, and protection, ensuring the victory of good over evil within and without.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raghubir: Beloved of God (Raghu) or Rama (God in human form), bearing divine joy (Bir).
